instruction: Modify the VLC progress slider so its colors are darker and less distracting than the current default.

command: import pyautogui; import time; pyautogui.click({SCREEN_WIDTH_HALF}, {SCREEN_HEIGHT_HALF}); time.sleep(0.5);

metadata.explanation: Task requires changing VLC slider colors to a darker color scheme (qt-slider-colours should contain RGB values where all colors are blackish, i.e., all RGB components < 100). Evaluator uses existing check_qt_slider_colours metric with type='blackish' and get_vlc_config getter to read VLC configuration file and verify all slider colors have low RGB values (< 100 threshold). Default colors are bright (e.g., 153;210;153;20;210;20;255;199;15;245;39;29), so the agent must navigate to Tools > Preferences > Interface > Customize colors and set darker colors. This is similar in complexity to the original task (changing a single VLC configuration setting).

llm_judge_reasons: Getter logic is correct: get_vlc_config reads the VLC configuration file (vlcrc) and returns the file path, which is appropriate for extracting VLC settings

Metric logic is correct: check_qt_slider_colours with type='blackish' correctly parses the qt-slider-colours setting and verifies all RGB components are below 100, which semantically matches 'darker, more subtle' colors
Complete coverage: The evaluator verifies the exact requirement from the instruction (changing slider colors to darker scheme)
Postconfig is appropriate: Restarts VLC to ensure the updated configuration is properly read from disk
Expected value handling is correct: The rule structure {'type': 'blackish'} is properly passed to the metric function and accessed correctly
Threshold is reasonable: RGB < 100 is a sensible threshold for 'blackish' colors, ensuring all slider colors are dark enough to qualify as 'darker, more subtle'
